FN-7KQ3VVV-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 220
Committee: County and Municipal Government Sponsor: Senator Dan Roberts
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/20/2024
Senate Bill 220 as introduced could increase receipts to the State General Fund from fines;
increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which court
costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district
attorneys, the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections, and community
corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons
charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.
In addition, this bill would increase the obligations of the Chief Procurement Officer, by an
undetermined amount to implement and administer the provisions of this
bill.
Page 1

FN-7KQ3VVV-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 220
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Dan Roberts
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 04/29/2024
Senate Bill 220 as passed the Senate could increase receipts to the State General Fund from
fines; increase receipts to the State General Fund, county general funds and other funds to which
court costs are deposited; and could increase the obligations of the State General Fund, district
attorneys, the Bureau of Pardons and Paroles, the Department of Corrections, and community
corrections programs by an undetermined amount dependent upon the number of persons
charged with and convicted of the offenses provided by the bill and the penalties imposed.
In addition, this bill would prohibit certain state and local governmental entities from
contracting with certain companies and increase the administrative obligations of the Chief
Procurement Officer to implement and administer the provisions of this bill.
Page 1

FN-7KQ3VVV-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 220
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Dan Roberts
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 05/01/2024
Senate Bill 220 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means General Fund would prohibit
certain state and local governmental entities from contracting with certain companies beginning
October 1, 2024.
